correctness.rationale: Every three-colouring with a colour on both parts is forced onto a single missing pair; two shared colours force exactly the three-pair six-cycle exception. This gives a complete state partition into six hypercubes and six square states per matching deletion. Junction rerouting proves base isometry, the Hamming-derived circle coordinate and route construction prove all eccentricities, and a winding argument gives odd girth. Two independently constructed exhaustive finite checkers passed the stated test domains including the boundary case; the infinite statements are justified by the written proof rather than finite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The primary earlier 2016 paper treats the no-deletion case, and earlier own work covered the single missing edge. Neither implies that arbitrarily many disjoint missing edges do not interact; the sharp three-pair six-cycle obstruction and stable all-state metrics distinguish the new family. Literature and mathematical-database searches by equivalent names identified no covering statement, subject to the enumerated residual risks.

value.rationale: The main value is a robust infinite-family transition: deleting arbitrarily many disjoint cross edges changes exactly six local state squares per edge but not the sharp metric or all-state eccentricity, until an isolated-state failure precisely at the six-cycle. This resolves a natural interaction question not answered by existing no-deletion and one-deletion classifications. The exact graphical model provides a benchmark for colour-reconfiguration algorithms and Glauber dynamics without claiming a mixing-time result.
